blocking_findings.issue: Chess inaccuracy in 'A useful comparison to keep': 'A pinned piece may be unable to capture the line piece because that capture would expose its king.' Capturing the pinning piece along the pin line never exposes the king, because it removes the attacker. A pinned piece fails to capture the pinner only when it cannot move along that line (a pinned knight, or a bishop pinned on a file or rank). The sentence also blurs 'line piece' with 'the attacker's support'.
blocking_findings.suggested_correction: Replace with: 'A pinned piece can capture the pinning piece only if it moves along the pin line. A rook pinned on a file by a rook can take it, but a pinned knight, or a bishop pinned on a file, cannot. If the pinner is supported, check whether that capture simply loses the piece to a recapture.'

blocking_findings.issue: Chess inaccuracy: 'An opposing king often cannot capture it without meeting that protecting pawn.' A king can never capture a protected pawn, because that would be moving into check. The word 'often' turns a rule into a tendency and misleads beginners.
blocking_findings.suggested_correction: Replace with: 'While its support remains, the opposing king cannot legally capture it. The defender must first eliminate or undermine the protecting pawn, so the passer can restrict the king's activity.'

blocking_findings.suggested_correction: Shorten it to a complete sentence under about 155 characters, e.g. 'Identify the real threat before chasing an early queen, develop with tempo when it is safe, and check which squares your move leaves undefended.'

Template signals that read as thin, scaled content: the identical heading 'A useful comparison to keep' appears in every sampled tactics, calculation and positional guide, and its contents often are not a comparison; 'A deliberate practice task' is likewise identical across guides. Give each section a specific heading.

Template signals in metadata: the lede duplicates the description verbatim in most guides. Several pages share identical related-link triples (puzzle-rating-vs-chess-rating and chess-training-vs-online-play; choose-iphone-chess-app and choose-chess-computer-strength). The whole study-plans cluster cites the same two generic sources (Chess.com study plan directory, lichess.org/features), even where a specific source fits better (e.g. a Lichess puzzle or rating page for the puzzle-rating guide).

Many guides lean heavily on hedges ('This is not a promise...', 'not a conversational AI tutor', 'not a built-in engine-versus-engine tournament'). The disclaimers are accurate, but repeating them in nearly every appFit reads as defensive. Keep one clear limitation per appFit and drop pre-emptive negations of features nobody asked about.

Several samples lack a wordCount field (tactics, calculation, positional, endgame, opening). At roughly 475-505 words, guides are at the thin end for 'deep' guide intent. The best candidates for one worked example from a real or study position are pin-versus-skewer-training, key-squares-pawn-endings and fifty-move-rule.

fifty-move-rule is accurate on FIDE 9.3 and 9.6.2, including checkmate taking precedence on the 75th move. Optionally note that the claim can be made when about to play the move that completes the fifty, by writing it on the scoresheet and declaring the intention to the arbiter.

Spelling consistency: titles and body use British spelling ('centre', 'analyse', 'practise'), while some keywords use US forms ('chess center control'). Align the visible title and keyword choice deliberately, without adding volume claims.

defend-early-queen-attacks: confirm that https://lichess.org/page/fair-play resolves. If not, cite Lichess's Terms of Service or fair-play FAQ page directly. Also confirm https://support.chess.com/en/articles/8583757-how-do-i-use-game-analysis in chess-engine-analysis-workflow.
verdict: revise_before_publish: two chess-accuracy errors (pin capture legality, protected-pawn capture), one truncated description, malformed primary-reference Lichess URLs, one confirmed and one likely intent overlap, and an unverified 'positional exercises' app claim must be fixed. The remaining samples are chess-accurate, avoid volume and ranking claims, and keep fair-play and app limits (local engines, daily free training limits, 15 endgame drills, no FEN editor, no LLM tutor) correctly stated.
